title: Many epochs on one batch
goal:
Implement the inner loop of Algorithm 1 (Section 5) for a softmax policy over $K$ arms with no state: collect one batch, then run $K_{epochs}$ epochs of gradient ascent on $L^{CLIP}$ using that same batch. The parameters are the logits `theta`.

Write `ppo_epochs(theta_old, actions, adv, eps, lr, epochs)`. It returns the new logits and doesn't change `theta_old`. Each epoch is one full-batch gradient step: `theta = theta + lr * grad`. The probability ratio always compares the current policy with the fixed old policy from the start of the call. Passing `eps=None` uses the unclipped objective $L^{CPI}$ (Equation 6).

The starter gives you `softmax` and the finished `clip_grad_logp`, which returns $\partial L / \partial \log\pi_\theta(a_t)$ for each sample (Exercise 1). You write the chain rule from log-probabilities to logits and the loop. For a softmax policy, $\partial \log\pi_\theta(a) / \partial\theta = \mathrm{onehot}(a) - \pi_\theta$.
hints: Compute `logp_old = np.log(softmax(theta_old))[actions]` once, before the loop. If you recompute it each epoch, the ratio is always 1 and clipping never triggers.

Inside the loop, `g = clip_grad_logp(np.log(pi)[actions], logp_old, adv, eps)` has shape `(N,)`. The logit gradient is `g @ (onehot - pi)`, where `onehot = np.eye(K)[actions]` has shape `(N, K)` and `pi` broadcasts over the rows.
With one epoch the ratio is exactly 1, so the step equals the vanilla policy gradient step, which is $\mathrm{lr} \cdot \frac1N\sum_t \hat A_t(\mathrm{onehot}(a_t) - \pi)$.
Copy `theta_old` into a new float array before the loop.
